title: Prime number check
idea: A prime has exactly two divisors: 1 and itself. Test divisors only up to √n — if none divides n, it is prime.

title: Palindrome check
idea: A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards. Compare the text with its reverse (for numbers, reverse the digits).

title: Fibonacci series
idea: Each term is the sum of the previous two: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5 … Keep two variables and slide them forward in a loop.

code.python:
n = 10
a, b = 0, 1
for _ in range(n):
    print(a, end=" ")
    a, b = b, a + b
print()

title: Factorial (loop)
idea: n! = 1 × 2 × … × n. Start with 1 and multiply in a loop. (Ask me "recursion" for the recursive version.)

code.python:
n = 5
fact = 1
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    fact *= i
print(f"{n}! = {fact}")

title: Reverse a number
idea: Repeatedly take the last digit with `% 10`, append it to the result (`rev * 10 + digit`), and drop it with integer division by 10.

code.python:
n = 12345
rev = 0
while n > 0:
    rev = rev * 10 + n % 10
    n //= 10
print("Reversed:", rev)

title: Sum of digits
idea: Take the last digit with `% 10`, add it, remove it with `// 10` (or `/ 10` for ints) until the number becomes 0.

code.python:
n = 9875
total = 0
while n > 0:
    total += n % 10
    n //= 10
print("Sum of digits:", total)

title: Armstrong number
idea: A number is Armstrong if the sum of each digit raised to the power of the number of digits equals the number (153 = 1³ + 5³ + 3³).

title: Leap year check
idea: A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4 **and** not by 100 — unless it is also divisible by 400.

code.javascript:
const isLeap = (y) => (y % 4 === 0 && y % 100 !== 0) || y % 400 === 0;
for (const y of [2024, 1900, 2000, 2023]) console.log(y, isLeap(y) ? "leap" : "not leap");

output:
2024 leap
1900 not leap
2000 leap
2023 not leap

title: Even or odd
idea: A number is even when the remainder after dividing by 2 is 0: `n % 2 == 0`.

code.python:
for n in [7, 10, 0, -3]:
    print(n, "is", "even" if n % 2 == 0 else "odd")

output:
7 is odd
10 is even
0 is even
-3 is odd

title: Largest of three numbers
idea: Compare with if / else-if — or use the built-in max function.

title: Swap two numbers
idea: Use a temporary variable (works everywhere). Python can swap in one line with tuple unpacking.

code.python:
a, b = 5, 9
print("Before:", a, b)
a, b = b, a          # tuple unpacking
print("After:", a, b)

title: GCD (HCF) and LCM
idea: Euclid's algorithm: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b is 0. Then lcm = a × b / gcd.

code.python:
def gcd(a, b):
    while b:
        a, b = b, a % b
    return a

a, b = 12, 18
g = gcd(a, b)
print("GCD:", g)
print("LCM:", a * b // g)

title: Count vowels in a string
idea: Loop over each character and check whether it is in "aeiou" (after converting to lowercase).

code.python:
s = "Programming Is Fun"
vowels = sum(1 for ch in s.lower() if ch in "aeiou")
print("Vowels:", vowels)

title: Reverse a string
idea: Python: slicing `s[::-1]`. JavaScript: split → reverse → join. Java: `StringBuilder.reverse()`. C++: `reverse()` from `<algorithm>`. Or build it yourself with a loop from the end.

code.python:
s = "coding"
print(s[::-1])
rev = ""
for ch in s:
    rev = ch + rev       # manual way
print(rev)

title: Multiplication table
idea: A single loop from 1 to 10, printing `n × i` on each line.

code.javascript:
const n = 7;
for (let i = 1; i <= 10; i++) console.log(`${n} x ${i} = ${n * i}`);

title: Sum of first n natural numbers
idea: Add 1..n in a loop — or use the formula n × (n + 1) / 2.

code.python:
n = 100
total = 0
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    total += i
print("Loop:", total)
print("Formula:", n * (n + 1) // 2)

title: Anagram check
idea: Two words are anagrams if they contain the same letters the same number of times — sort both and compare.

title: Second largest element
idea: Track the largest and second-largest values in one pass (skip duplicates of the largest).
